The invention relates to a system for monitoring the position of an injection-molding machine’s closing unit while the light curtain protecting the closing unit and tool area is temporarily bypassed. The injection-molding machine includes at least one molding tool comprising at least two tool parts that, when closed, enclose one or more mold cavities.

A programmable logic controller (PLC) controls a movement-monitoring module that indirectly monitors both the movement of the closing unit and the relative positions of the molding-tool parts. Distance-measuring sticks are used as position sensors. Their measurement signals are transmitted to the PLC and evaluated through the movement-monitoring module.

During the bumping step, the relative spacing between the tool parts is continuously monitored. The tool parts must remain within a predefined maximum gap. If the measured spacing exceeds this permitted value, the monitoring system initiates an automatic machine shutdown to prevent hazardous movement while the protective light curtain is bypassed.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a safety system for monitoring an injection-molding machine, particularly the closing unit and the relative positions of the mold parts when the machine is operated with the safety light curtain temporarily bypassed. One or more distance-measuring sensors are arranged to continuously detect the position of the movable closing unit and/or the distance between the mold parts. The sensor signals are transmitted to a movement-monitoring module controlled by a programmable logic controller (PLC), which evaluates the measured positions and compares them with predefined permissible values throughout the relevant machine cycle.

Special monitoring is performed during the post-filling bumping step, in which pressure is applied after the mold has been filled. During this step, the system determines whether the gap between the mold parts remains within a specified maximum limit. If the measured gap exceeds that limit, or if the detected movement otherwise falls outside the permitted range, the monitoring module immediately initiates a safe shutdown of the injection-molding machine. This prevents continued operation under potentially hazardous conditions despite the light curtain being bypassed. By providing independent, position-based supervision of the closing unit and mold parts, the invention increases personnel and machine safety while permitting the required production or setup operation to be carried out.
outputs.L5:
## The Role of PLCs in MOC Processes

A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is a critical component in many industrial automation systems. It controls machinery, monitors operating conditions, and helps maintain safe and efficient production. Because PLC programs directly affect industrial processes, any modification must be carefully planned and documented.

Management of Change (MOC) provides a structured method for evaluating and approving these modifications. An MOC process may be required when changing PLC logic, alarm settings, safety interlocks, communication networks, or connected equipment. Before implementation, the proposed change should undergo a risk assessment, technical review, testing, and formal authorization.

The PLC and MOC processes must work together to protect personnel, equipment, and production. Proper documentation, version control, backups, employee training, and post-change verification help ensure that every PLC modification is introduced safely and reliably.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the technical abstract of a patent for an injection-molding machine safety system that indirectly monitors mold position after closing pressure is applied and the mold cavity is filled.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A safety system for an injection-molding machine indirectly monitors mold position after application of mold-closing pressure and filling of a mold cavity. One or more sensors detect an operating parameter correlated with relative movement or separation of mold members, including clamp force, tie-bar strain, hydraulic pressure, actuator position, platen deformation, or a combination thereof. A controller establishes a reference value after the mold reaches a closed condition and evaluates sensor data during and/or after injection against a predetermined threshold or permissible profile. A change indicating that the mold position has deviated from the closed condition causes the controller to initiate a safety response, such as inhibiting further injection, reducing cavity or holding pressure, stopping machine operation, retracting an injection unit, or generating an alarm. The system thereby detects mold opening or displacement under cavity pressure without requiring a position sensor to directly measure a gap between the mold members.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention notes into formal patent language: injection-molding machine; two-part molding tool; light-curtain bypass; PLC-controlled MOC; distance sensors; maximum permitted spacing gap during the bumping step; automatic shutdown when exceeded.
counterfactuals.output:
### Title  
**Injection-Molding Machine Having Distance-Monitored Safety Control During a Tool-Bumping Operation**

### Abstract  
An injection-molding machine includes a molding tool having first and second tool parts movable relative to one another, a programmable logic controller configured to control a mold opening-and-closing operation, and a safety light curtain protecting an access region of the molding tool. During a controlled tool-bumping operation, a safety controller conditionally mutes the light curtain while one or more distance sensors monitor a spacing gap between the first and second tool parts. The safety controller compares the measured spacing gap with a predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap. If the measured spacing gap exceeds the maximum permitted spacing gap, the safety controller automatically terminates movement of the molding tool and places the injection-molding machine in a safe state.

### Exemplary Independent Claim  
1. **An injection-molding machine comprising:**  
   
   a molding tool including a first tool part and a second tool part movable relative to the first tool part;  
   
   a drive system configured to move at least one of the first and second tool parts during a mold opening-and-closing operation;  
   
   a programmable logic controller operatively coupled to the drive system and configured to control the mold opening-and-closing operation;  
   
   a light-curtain safety device arranged to monitor an access region associated with the molding tool;  
   
   at least one distance sensor configured to generate a signal representative of a spacing gap between the first tool part and the second tool part; and  
   
   a safety controller configured to:  
   
   permit a controlled muting of the light-curtain safety device during a tool-bumping step;  
   
   receive the signal generated by the at least one distance sensor;  
   
   compare the spacing gap represented by the signal with a predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap for the tool-bumping step; and  
   
   in response to determining that the spacing gap exceeds the predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap, automatically stop movement of the molding tool and place the injection-molding machine in a safe operating state.

### Exemplary Dependent Claims  
2. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the safety controller permits the controlled muting only while the spacing gap is less than or equal to the predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap.

3. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the at least one distance sensor comprises two mutually redundant distance sensors.

4. The injection-molding machine of claim 3, wherein the safety controller is configured to initiate the safe operating state when signals from the two distance sensors differ by more than a predetermined tolerance.

5. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the safe operating state comprises removing motive power from the drive system, applying a brake, closing a hydraulic control valve, inhibiting further mold movement, or a combination thereof.

6. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the safety controller is separate from the programmable logic controller and communicates with the programmable logic controller through a safety-rated communication interface.

7. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the tool-bumping step comprises incremental relative movement of the first and second tool parts for installation, alignment, testing, maintenance, or setup of the molding tool.

8. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein the predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap is stored as a configurable machine parameter and is changeable only through an access-controlled setup procedure.

9. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein interruption of the light curtain outside the controlled muting condition causes automatic termination of movement of the molding tool.

10. The injection-molding machine of claim 1, wherein a fault, loss of signal, or implausible measurement from the at least one distance sensor causes the safety controller to place the injection-molding machine in the safe operating state.

### Exemplary Method Claim  
11. **A method for controlling an injection-molding machine having a two-part molding tool, the method comprising:**  
   
   initiating, under control of a programmable logic controller, a tool-bumping step in which first and second tool parts are moved relative to one another;  
   
   conditionally muting a light-curtain safety device during the tool-bumping step;  
   
   measuring, by at least one distance sensor, a spacing gap between the first and second tool parts;  
   
   comparing the measured spacing gap with a predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap; and  
   
   automatically stopping movement of the molding tool and placing the injection-molding machine in a safe state when the measured spacing gap exceeds the predetermined maximum permitted spacing gap.

12. The method of claim 11, further comprising automatically restoring the light-curtain safety device to an active monitoring state upon completion or interruption of the tool-bumping step.

### Specification-Style Description  
In one embodiment, the injection-molding machine is equipped with a two-part molding tool whose tool parts are displaced relative to one another by a hydraulic, electric, or electromechanical drive. A programmable logic controller controls the mold opening-and-closing operation, including a setup or tool-bumping mode in which limited incremental movement of the tool parts is permitted.

Access to the molding region is monitored by a light curtain. During the tool-bumping mode, interruption of the light curtain may be conditionally disregarded or muted only under predetermined safety conditions. One or more distance sensors continuously or cyclically determine the spacing gap between the tool parts. The measured spacing gap is supplied to a safety controller and compared with a stored maximum permitted spacing gap.

So long as the measured spacing gap does not exceed the maximum permitted spacing gap and all additional safety conditions remain satisfied, the safety controller may permit continued execution of the tool-bumping step. If the measured spacing gap exceeds the maximum permitted spacing gap, or if a sensor or communication fault occurs, the safety controller automatically disables the drive, arrests movement of the tool parts, and inhibits further machine operation until a prescribed reset procedure has been completed.
